title: Web Crawler
statement:
Write `crawl(startUrl, htmlParser)`, a web crawler that returns every page reachable from `startUrl` without leaving its hostname. The only way to read a page is `htmlParser.getUrls(url)`, which returns the list of urls that the page `url` links to. The rules:

- Begin at `startUrl` and follow links, but only to urls whose hostname equals the hostname of `startUrl`; never call `getUrls` for a url on another hostname.
- Crawl each url at most once: never call `getUrls` twice with the same url.
- Every url has the form `http://hostname` or `http://hostname/path` with no port, so its hostname is the text between `http://` and the next `/` (or the end). Hostnames must match exactly: `leetcode.com`, `a.leetcode.com` and `leetcode.com.cn` are three different hostnames.
- Return `startUrl` and every same-hostname url you reached, each once, in any order.

Each case gives `urls`, `edges` and `startUrl`: `edges[j] = [a, b]` means that the page `urls[a]` links to `urls[b]`. Your function receives only `startUrl` and `htmlParser`, which answers from those links; the judge rejects a solution that breaks one of the two `getUrls` rules above.
constraints: The urls are distinct and have the form http://hostname or http://hostname/path, with no port
A hostname is 1 to 63 characters of lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens, and does not start or end with a hyphen
edges[j] = [a, b] with 0 <= a, b < urls.length
signature: List<String> crawl(String[] urls, int[][] edges, String startUrl)
api: crawl(startUrl: string, htmlParser: { getUrls(url: string): string[] }): string[]
notes:
## Intuition

The pages form a directed graph: each url is a node and each link is an edge. Crawling means finding every node reachable from `startUrl`, except that a page on another hostname is a wall: it may not be opened, so links behind it do not count. A breadth-first search does exactly this, as long as foreign urls are never put in the queue and every url is marked the first time it is seen. (The brute force does the same walk depth-first, with a linear search for "seen".)

## Approach

1. Define `hostname(url)` as the third piece of `url.split('/')`: splitting `http://a.com/x` gives `"http:"`, `""`, `"a.com"`, `"x"`. Store the start page's hostname in `host`.
2. Put `startUrl` in `seen` and in `queue`, and read the queue from index `front`.
3. Take the next `url` and call `getUrls(url)` once for it.
4. Skip each `link` that is already in `seen` or whose hostname is not `host`.
5. Otherwise add the link to `seen` and to `queue`, so it is crawled later.
6. When the queue is used up, return everything in `seen`.

## Example 1, step by step

`startUrl` is `http://news.yahoo.com/news/topics/`, so `host = "news.yahoo.com"`.

- Crawl `/news/topics/`: it links to `http://news.yahoo.com` and `/news`; both are new and on `host`, so both are queued.
- Crawl `http://news.yahoo.com`: it links to `/us`, which is new: queue it.
- Crawl `/news` and `/us`: neither has links.
- The queue is empty. `http://news.google.com` was never reached (it links to the others, but nothing links to it), so the answer is the four `news.yahoo.com` urls.

## Complexity

- Time: O(V + E) hostname checks and set operations (times the url length), where V is the number of crawled pages and E the number of links they hold.
- Space: O(V) for `seen` and `queue`.

## Pitfalls

- Comparing hostnames with `startsWith` or `includes`: `leetcode.com.cn`, `a.leetcode.com` and `http://other.com/leetcode.com` all contain `leetcode.com`.
- Marking a url only when it is crawled instead of when it is queued: a page linked from two crawled pages would then be queued, and fetched, twice.
- A same-hostname page linked only from a foreign page is not reachable, because the foreign page may not be opened.
- `http://t.co/x` and `http://t.co/x/` are different urls; do not normalise them.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hostname` | returns the hostname part of a url |
| `host` | the hostname of `startUrl`; only urls with it are crawled |
| `seen` | every url already discovered, which is also the answer |
| `queue` | urls waiting to be crawled, in discovery order |
| `front` | index of the next url to take from `queue` |
| `url`, `link` | the page being crawled and one of its links |

narration.2: The hostname is the third piece when splitting on "/": "http:", "", then the host.
narration.3: Only pages on the start page's hostname may be crawled.
narration.4: Mark startUrl as discovered so no link leads back to it twice.
narration.5: The BFS queue starts with the first page to crawl.
narration.7: Keep crawling while some discovered page has not been read yet.
narration.8: Take the oldest page that is still waiting.
narration.10: Read the page once and look at each of its links.
narration.11: Ignore links already discovered and links to other hostnames.
narration.14: Mark the link as discovered as soon as it is found, not when it is crawled.
narration.15: Queue it so its own links are read later.
narration.18: Every discovered url is on the right hostname and reachable, so return them all.
